newsitem.title: USA: Economists divided on Fed money market move Tues.
newsitem.headline: Economists divided on Fed money market move Tues.

text.p: Economists were divided as to whether the Federal Reserve would intervene in the money market Tuesday morning.

Some thought the Fed could remain out of the banking system while one looked for a round of term system repurchase agreements that runs into next week. Monday the Fed injected reserves with a round of 10-day fixed system repos.

"Our reserve forecasts show the Fed with an add need of about $11.5 billion a day in the first half of the current maintenance period ending Jan. 15," said James Blumenthal, economist at MCM Moneywatch.

With the 13-day outstanding system repo running off the books on Wednesday, the Fed will opt for a short-term system repo to help meet the projected $10 billion a day add need in the second half of the period, he said.
However, economists at UBS Securities Inc and MMS International argued the Fed's add need had been adequately addressed and it would remain out of the market Tuesday.
The federal funds rate was trading at 5-13/16 percent, near the current target level of 5.25 percent.
-- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury Desk, 212-859-1663
